mainTopic: Honoring and fearing parents: the order of father and mother in the פסוקים, God's presence, whose request comes first, the stories of דמא בן נתינה, and why being commanded makes a מצוה greater
overview: This amud is all about honoring and fearing parents. It opens by finishing a ברייתא: the תורה lists the father first for כיבוד (honor) but the mother first for מורא (fear), to strengthen whichever one a child would naturally give less of. Then come sayings about God's presence: God 'does not dwell' with people who hurt their parents, sinning in secret is like pushing away the שכינה, and one should not walk arrogantly or bareheaded. A widow's son asks whose request comes first, and רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע both say the father comes first, because the mother also owes him honor. If the parents are divorced, they are treated equally. עולא רבה and רבא then show that the commandment to honor parents proved to the nations that all of God's words are sincere. Next, the גמרא asks how far כיבוד אב ואם goes and answers with stories about דמא בן נתינה, a gentile who gave up a fortune rather than wake his father and stayed silent when his mother shamed him. From his reward, רבי חנינא teaches that one who is commanded and does is greater than one who is not commanded, which makes the blind רב יוסף change his mind. The amud ends as אבימי begins a teaching that a son can feed his father fine food and still be punished, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the father is listed first for honor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its reason: a mother wins her son over with gentle words, so he honors her more naturally. Therefore the תורה put כיבוד אב first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the mother persuades him with gentle words, הקדוש ברוך הוא put כיבוד אב before כיבוד אם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that already began on the previous page. It explains why the פסוק of כיבוד mentions the father first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son naturally honors his mother more, because she is gentle and speaks kindly to him. So the תורה puts the father first, to stress the parent the son would tend to neglect. The order in the פסוק pushes against natural human tendency.

phrases.english: because she persuades him with words,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the mother. This sentence started on the previous page.

phrases.english: therefore the Holy One, Blessed be He, put first
honor of the father before honor of the mother.
phrases.notes: שמות 20:11, 'Honor your father and your mother.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ הִקְדִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כִּיבּוּד אָב לְכִיבּוּד אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father is listed first for honor because the son naturally honors his mother more.

steps.title: Why the mother is listed first for fear
steps.stepSummary: God knows a son fears his father more, because the father teaches him תורה. So the פסוק of מורא puts the mother first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that a son fears his father more than his mother, because the father teaches him תורה. Therefore הקדוש ברוך הוא put מורא of the mother before מורא of the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the matching reason for the second פסוק: why the mother comes first when the תורה commands fear (מורא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the situation is reversed. The father is strict, because he teaches his son תורה, so the son already fears him. The תורה therefore puts the mother first, again stressing the parent who would naturally get less.

keyTerms.meaning: the One Who spoke and the world came to be (a name for God)

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה switches the order on purpose. Father comes first for honor and mother comes first for fear, to strengthen whichever one a child would naturally give less of.

phrases.english: And it is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came into being
that a son fears his father more than his mother,
because he teaches him Torah,
therefore the Holy One, Blessed be He, put first
fear of the mother before fear of the father.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3, 'A man shall fear his mother and his father.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגָלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second half of the same ברייתא, applying the same logic to מורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother is listed first for fear because the son naturally fears his father more.

steps.title: God avoids dwelling with those who hurt their parents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught before רב נחמן: when someone causes his parents pain, God says it is good He did not dwell among them, or they would have hurt Him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: When a person causes pain to his father and mother, הקדוש ברוך הוא says: I did well not to live among them, because if I had lived among them, they would have caused Me pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the seriousness of hurting one's parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parents are partners with God in making a child. So how a person treats his parents shows how he would treat God. Someone who hurts his parents would hurt God too, if God were close by.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter of ברייתות taught before (a sage)

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:
phrases.notes: Here a 'tanna' is someone whose job was to memorize ברייתות and recite them in the study hall.

phrases.english: When a person causes pain to
his father and his mother,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, says:
I did well that I did not dwell among them,
for had I dwelled among them, they would have caused Me pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of the פסוקים to the seriousness of hurting one's parents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Causing one's parents pain is treated as if it causes pain to God.

steps.title: Sinning in secret pushes away the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that sinning in private is like pushing away the feet of the שכינה. He brings a פסוק calling the earth God's footstool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: Anyone who sins in secret is as if he pushes away the feet of the שכינה, as it says: 'So says ה׳: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds another teaching about God's presence. A secret sin acts as if God is not there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God's 'feet' rest on the whole earth, so He is present everywhere. A person who hides in order to sin is acting as if God is not in that place. It is as though he shoves God's feet away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
Anyone who commits a sin in secret,
it is as if he pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence.
As it says: 'So says ה׳:
The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה בַּסֵּתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of how human behavior affects God's presence among people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A secret sin is like pushing away the שכינה, since God is present everywhere on earth.

steps.title: Do not walk with an arrogant, upright posture
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids walking even four אמות with an arrogant, stiff-upright posture, because the whole world is full of God's glory.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: It is forbidden for a person to walk four cubits with an upright posture, as it says: 'The whole earth is full of His glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a practical rule that comes from the same idea: God's presence is everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since God's glory fills every place, walking proudly with a stiff, raised stance shows no awareness that one stands before Him. Even a short distance of four אמות counts.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean you must walk hunched over. 'קומה זקופה' means a proud, haughty way of walking, not simply standing up straight.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
It is forbidden for a person to walk four cubits
with an upright posture,
as it says: 'The whole earth is full of His glory.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיְּהַלֵּךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the idea of God's presence everywhere into a practical rule about how to walk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to walk four אמות in an arrogant upright posture.

steps.title: רב הונא would not walk bareheaded
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע would not walk four אמות with his head uncovered, because the שכינה is above his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, would not walk four אמות with his head uncovered. He said: The שכינה is above my head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us about one אמורא's personal practice that comes from the same awareness of God's presence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the previous step: if God's glory is everywhere, then it is right above me too. רב הונא showed respect by covering his head even for a short walk.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic early source for the Jewish practice of covering one's head.

phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מְסַגֵּי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בְּגִילּוּי הָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: would not walk four cubits with an uncovered head.
He said: The Divine Presence is above my head.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לָא מְסַגֵּי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בְּגִילּוּי הָרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a personal practice that fits the same idea as רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא would not walk four אמות bareheaded, out of awareness of the שכינה above him.

steps.title: A widow's son asks: whose request comes first?
steps.stepSummary: A widow's son asks רבי אליעזר: if both father and mother ask me for water, which one do I serve first?
steps.simpleTranslation: The son of a certain widow asked רבי אליעזר: If Father says, 'Give me water to drink,' and Mother says, 'Give me water to drink,' which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to honoring parents. It presents a practical question: what to do when both parents ask at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the father and mother are equal in honor and fear. Now a real conflict comes up: the son can only serve one first. The question is which parent gets priority.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל בֶּן אַלְמָנָה אַחַת אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: The son of a certain widow asked Rabbi Eliezer:
If Father says: 'Give me water to drink,'
and Mother says: 'Give me water to drink,'
which of them comes first?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל בֶּן אַלְמָנָה אַחַת אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to כיבוד אב ואם with a practical conflict between the two parents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When father and mother make the same request at the same time, whose honor takes priority?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the father comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the son should set aside his mother's honor and serve his father, because both he and his mother are obligated to honor the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Set aside the honor of your mother and do the honor of your father, because you and your mother are both obligated in the honor of your father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question: the father's request comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not that the mother matters less. Rather, the mother herself is obligated to honor her husband. So when the son serves the father, he is also doing what his mother is supposed to do, and the honor of both parents points to the father.

phrases.english: He said to him: Set aside the honor of your mother
and do the honor of your father,
for you and your mother are both obligated in the honor of your father.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנַּח כְּבוֹד אִמְּךָ וַעֲשֵׂה כְּבוֹד אָבִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the widow's son's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father comes first, because the mother is also obligated in the father's honor.

steps.title: רבי יהושע gives the same answer
steps.stepSummary: The son goes to רבי יהושע with the same question and gets the same answer. This sets up his follow-up question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי יהושע, and he told him the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The son checks with a second sage and gets the same ruling. This line also sets up his next question to רבי יהושע, which comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great sages agree that the father comes first. Having heard the same answer twice, the son now has the setting to ask a deeper follow-up question to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yehoshua,
and he told him the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לוֹ כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רבי אליעזר's answer through a second sage and prepares the follow-up question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע also rules that the father comes first.

steps.title: The son asks: What if my mother were divorced?
steps.stepSummary: The widow's son follows up: if the mother is divorced from the father, who comes first?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, if she is divorced, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The widow's son asks a follow-up question to רבי יהושע: what if the parents are divorced? This sets up רבי יהושע's sharp answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said the father comes first because the mother herself must honor the father. Once a woman is divorced, she no longer owes her ex-husband that honor. So the son is asking whether the father still comes first.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
if she is divorced, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, נִתְגָּרְשָׁה מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up to the answer of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע: tests whether their reason still applies after a divorce.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the parents are divorced, which parent is served first?

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers with gentle mockery: treat them equally
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע notes that the man is clearly a widow's son, so the question doesn't apply to him. Then he gives a sarcastic answer: serve them both at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From your eyelashes it is clear that you are a widow's son. Pour water for them into a basin and cluck at them as you would at chickens.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע points out that the man's father is dead, so his question is not practical for him. Then he answers mockingly: just set out water for both of them like you feed chickens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His tears show he is a widow's son, so asking about a divorced mother is only theory. The joke answer has a real point: once the parents are divorced, the reason to put the father first is gone. Neither parent comes first, so serve them both together.
steps.whatToRemember: When parents are married, the father comes first, because the mother also must honor him. When they are divorced, both get equal honor.

phrases.english: He said to him: From between your eyelashes
it is clear that you are a widow's son.
phrases.notes: His eyes are wet from mourning. Your father has died, so why ask about divorce?

phrases.english: Pour water for them into a basin
and cluck at them as you would at chickens.
phrases.notes: It's a joke, but the meaning is real: after a divorce, neither parent comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִבֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינֶיךָ נִיכָּר שֶׁבֶּן אַלְמָנָה אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the divorce question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the parents are divorced, they are equal. The son serves both together, and neither comes first.

steps.title: The nations accepted God's first commandments once they heard 'Honor your father'
steps.stepSummary: עולא רבה explains why the verse says 'words' (plural). The nations thought God's first commandments were self-serving, until the commandment to honor parents showed they were true.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא רבה expounded at the entrance of the נשיא's house: What does it mean that it is written, 'All the kings of the earth shall thank You, ה׳, for they have heard the words of Your mouth'? It does not say 'the word of Your mouth' but 'the words of Your mouth.' When הקדוש ברוך הוא said 'I am' and 'You shall have no other gods,' the nations said: He demands this for His own honor. Once He said 'Honor your father and your mother,' they went back and admitted that the first statements were true.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא רבה explains a פסוק in תהלים about the kings of the earth thanking God for 'the words of Your mouth.' He says the nations accepted all of God's words, even the first ones, once they saw He also commands honor for parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'words' means the kings thanked God for more than one statement. At first, 'I am ה׳' and 'no other gods' looked like God seeking honor for Himself. When He commanded honor for human parents, the nations saw He was not self-centered, so they accepted the earlier commandments too.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded or taught a lesson from a פסוק
The house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish community

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how important כיבוד אב ואם is. This מצוה is what showed the whole world that God's commandments are sincere.

phrases.english: Ulla the Great expounded
at the entrance of the Nasi's house:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"All the kings of the earth shall thank You, ה׳,
for they have heard the words of Your mouth"?
It does not say "the word of Your mouth" (singular),
but rather "the words of Your mouth" (plural):
When the Holy One, Blessed be He, said
"I am" and "You shall have no other gods,"
phrases.notes: These are the first two of the עשרת הדברות, in שמות 20.

phrases.english: the nations of the world said:
He demands this for His own honor.
Once He said:
"Honor your father and your mother,"
they went back and admitted
that the first statements were true.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ עוּלָּא רַבָּה אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about how great כיבוד אב ואם is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The commandment to honor parents showed the nations that God's first commandments were sincere, so they accepted all His words.

steps.title: רבא's source: the end of God's word proves the beginning
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a different פסוק for the same idea: the later commandments show that the earlier ones are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It comes from here: 'The beginning of Your word is truth.' Is only the beginning of Your word true, and not the end? Rather, from the end of Your word it becomes clear that the beginning of Your word is truth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second פסוק that teaches the same lesson as עולא רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to praise only the beginning of God's word, which can't be right. So רבא reads it this way: the later commandments, like honoring parents, show that the first ones are true. It is the same idea from a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this other source

phrases.english: Rava said: It comes from here:
"The beginning of Your word is truth."
Only "the beginning of Your word," and not "the end of Your word"?
Rather, from the end of Your word it becomes clear
that the beginning of Your word is truth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the idea עולא רבה taught in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The later commandments show that the earlier commandments are true.

steps.title: How far does honoring parents go?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask רב עולא how far a person must go to honor his father and mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב עולא: How far must one go in honoring father and mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages ask רב עולא how far the מצוה of כיבוד אב ואם reaches. This sets up the story of דמא בן נתינה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is about the limit of the מצוה: how much must a person give up for his parents? The answer comes as a story, not a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of honoring father and mother

phrases.english: They asked Rav Ulla:
How far does honoring father and mother go?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב עוּלָּא: עַד הֵיכָן כִּיבּוּד אָב וָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the limits of the מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far a person must go to honor his parents.

steps.title: דמא בן נתינה gives up a fortune so as not to wake his father
steps.stepSummary: רב עולא answers with a story: a gentile in אשקלון gave up a deal worth 600,000 rather than wake his sleeping father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go and see what one gentile in אשקלון did, and his name was דמא בן נתינה. Once the Sages wanted to buy merchandise from him that would bring him a profit of 600,000. The key was lying under his father's head, and he did not disturb him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עולא answers with a story about דמא בן נתינה. He gave up a huge profit so he would not wake his father, who was sleeping on the key.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer shows how far the מצוה goes by example. A person should be ready to lose a great deal of money rather than cause his parent even small discomfort. A gentile who was not even commanded did this, so a Jew who is commanded should surely do at least as much.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and see, meaning learn from this example
Under his head, where he was lying
Troubled him or caused him discomfort

steps.confusionAlert: The next steps are not simply the rest of this telling. The גמרא brings a second version of the same story in רבי אליעזר's name (steps 16-17), and that version goes on to tell of the reward.

phrases.english: He said to them: Go out and see
what one gentile in Ashkelon did,
and his name was Dama ben Netina.
Once the Sages wanted to buy merchandise from him
that would bring a profit of six hundred thousand,
and the key was lying
under his father's head,
and he did not disturb him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מָה עָשָׂה נׇכְרִי אֶחָד בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person should give up even a huge profit rather than disturb his parent, as דמא בן נתינה did.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is asked how far honoring parents goes
steps.stepSummary: Through רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, the גמרא reports that רבי אליעזר was asked how far כיבוד אב ואם must go.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They asked רבי אליעזר, how far must a person go to honor his father and mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of the question from Step 14, now asked of רבי אליעזר. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question the Sages asked רב עולא, but it comes through a different chain of teachers. This new telling will add details the first one did not have.

keyTerms.meaning: How far? Up to what point?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They asked Rabbi Eliezer:
How far does honoring father and mother go?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: עַד הֵיכָן כִּיבּוּד אָב וָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of the question in Step 14, from a different chain of teachers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The extent of the obligation to honor parents.

steps.title: דמא בן נתינה would not wake his father for a huge deal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells of דמא בן נתינה, a gentile in אשקלון who gave up a huge profit on stones for the אפוד rather than disturb his father, who was sleeping on the key.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Go and see what one gentile in אשקלון, named דמא בן נתינה, did for his father. The Sages wanted to buy stones for the אפוד from him, with a profit of 600,000 (רב כהנא says 800,000). The key was under his sleeping father's head, and he would not disturb him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers with a real-life story instead of a rule. He shows how far honor goes through one gentile's sacrifice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version (step 15) already gave the name דמא בן נתינה and the key under his father's head. This version, in רבי אליעזר's name, adds that the Sages wanted stones for the אפוד. It also records רב כהנא's figure of 800,000 instead of 600,000. Either way the point is the same: he took a huge loss rather than bother his father.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the gentile in Ashkelon
The apron of the כהן גדול, set with precious stones

phrases.english: He said to them: Go out and see

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה נׇכְרִי אֶחָד לְאָבִיו בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן,
phrases.english: what one gentile did for his father in Ashkelon,
and Dama ben Netina was his name.
The Sages wanted stones from him for the Ephod
for a profit of six hundred thousand,
and Rav Kahana teaches: eight hundred thousand,
and the key was lying
under his father's head,
and he did not disturb him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מָה עָשָׂה נׇכְרִי אֶחָד לְאָבִיו בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Honor goes so far that one gives up a huge profit rather than disturb a sleeping parent.

steps.title: דמא is rewarded with a פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: A year later הקדוש ברוך הוא rewarded דמא with a פרה אדומה born in his herd. When the Sages came to buy it, he asked only for the money he had lost honoring his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year God gave him his reward: a red heifer was born in his herd. The Sages of Israel came to him. He said: I know that if I asked for all the money in the world, you would give it. But I ask only for the money I lost for my father's honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a new ending: God repays דמא for honoring his father. He refuses to overcharge and asks back only what he lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds something the first telling did not have: the reward. The Sages badly needed a פרה אדומה, so he could have charged anything. Instead he asked for exactly what honoring his father cost him, showing he did not regret it.

keyTerms.meaning: Red heifer, needed for purifying from טומאת מת and very rare

phrases.english: The next year
the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave him his reward,
as a red heifer was born to him in his herd.
The Sages of Israel came to him,
he said to them: I know about you
that if I ask from you

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָמוֹן שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם אַתֶּם נוֹתְנִין לִי,
phrases.english: all the money in the world, you would give it to me,
but I ask from you nothing
except that money which I lost
because of honoring Father.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשָׁנָה הָאַחֶרֶת נָתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of Step 17 with the reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God repaid דמא's sacrifice for his father with a פרה אדומה.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: if a gentile gets this, how much more a commanded Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא makes a קל וחומר from the story and grounds it in his rule: one who is commanded and does is greater than one who is not commanded and does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: If someone who is not commanded and does it gets such a reward, then someone who is commanded and does it, all the more so. For רבי חנינא said: Greater is one who is commanded and does than one who is not commanded and does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא draws a lesson from the story for Jews. Then the גמרא explains his reasoning by quoting his general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמא was a gentile, so he was not commanded to honor his parents, yet he got a big reward. רבי חנינא reasons that a Jew, who is commanded, gets even more. The quoted rule explains why: doing a מצוה you are commanded to do is a greater act.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is commanded and does it
One who is not commanded but does it anyway
All the more so (the ending of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's rule: גדול מצווה ועושה ממי שאינו מצווה ועושה. Being commanded makes the מצוה greater, not smaller.
steps.confusionAlert: It is easy to think doing something you don't have to do is more impressive. רבי חנינא says the opposite: the one who is commanded is greater.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for רב יוסף's change of heart in the next steps.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה וְעוֹשֶׂה – כָּךְ,
phrases.english: If one who is not commanded and does it gets this,
phrases.notes: This means דמא, a gentile who was not commanded to honor his father.

phrases.aramaic: מְצֻוֶּוה וְעוֹשֶׂה – עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: one who is commanded and does it, all the more so.
For Rabbi Chanina said:
Greater is one who is commanded and does it
than one who is not commanded and does it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה וְעוֹשֶׂה כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a קל וחומר from the reward in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is commanded and does is greater than one who is not commanded and does.

steps.title: רב יוסף's first thought: being exempt would be better
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, who was blind, says he used to think that if the הלכה followed רבי יהודה, who exempts a blind person from מצוות, he would celebrate, since he does them without being commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: At first I would say, if someone told me the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who says a blind person is exempt from מצוות, I would make a party for the Rabbis, since I am not commanded and yet I do them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells us his old opinion. The גמרא is setting up his change of mind in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף was blind. He thought being exempt and still keeping מצוות would earn him a bigger reward, so he hoped the הלכה followed רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: At first I would say:
Whoever would tell me
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
A blind person is exempt from the מצוות,
I would make a festive day for the Rabbis,
since I am not commanded, and yet I do them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that רבי חנינא's rule will overturn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף once thought that being exempt but still keeping מצוות was better.

steps.title: רב יוסף reverses: being commanded is better
steps.stepSummary: After hearing רבי חנינא's rule, רב יוסף says the opposite: he would celebrate if told the הלכה does NOT follow רבי יהודה, so that he is commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that I heard רבי חנינא's teaching, that one who is commanded and does is greater than one who is not commanded and does, the opposite is true: whoever tells me the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, I would make a party for the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף changes his mind because of רבי חנינא's rule. Now he wants to be obligated in מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being commanded makes a מצוה greater, then a blind person gains more by being obligated. So רב יוסף flips his wish completely. This shows how seriously the rule from Step 19 was taken.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's turnaround shows רבי חנינא's rule in action: it is a greater thing to be obligated in a מצוה and do it.

phrases.english: Now that I have heard this
that Rabbi Chanina said:
Greater is one who is commanded and does it
more than one who is not commanded and does it,
on the contrary:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לִי דְּאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: whoever tells me that the halacha is not like Rabbi Yehuda,
I would make a festive day for the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּשַׁמְעִיתַהּ לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רב יוסף's earlier view from Step 20 based on Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because one who is commanded and does is greater, רב יוסף would rather be obligated in מצוות.

steps.title: דמא בן נתינה stays silent when his mother humiliates him
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי tells that דמא בן נתינה, dressed in gold among the Roman nobles, was publicly shamed by his mother and did not embarrass her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: Once דמא was wearing a golden cloak and sitting among the nobles of Rome. His mother came, tore the cloak off him, hit him on the head, and spat in his face. Still, he did not embarrass her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי adds a second story about דמא בן נתינה. This one shows how far he went in honoring his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first story was about losing money. This story is about being shamed in public, in the most important company possible. דמא kept quiet and did not humiliate his mother in return, so honoring a parent includes holding back even when you are hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: When [he] came: the standard way the גמרא introduces a teaching brought from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A fine silk or ornate cloak
The nobles or great men of Rome

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיָה לָבוּשׁ סִירְקוֹן שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: Once he was wearing a cloak of gold,
phrases.notes: "He" is דמא בן נתינה, the gentile from the earlier stories.

phrases.english: and was sitting among the nobles of Rome.
And his mother came and tore it from him,
and smacked him on his head,
and spat in his face,
and he did not embarrass her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of רבי חנינא's rule and רב יוסף's reaction, the גמרא returns to דמא בן נתינה with another example of his כיבוד אב ואם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honoring a parent includes not shaming them back, even when they shame you in public.

steps.title: Feeding a father fine food can still lose a son his share in the next world
steps.stepSummary: אבימי בריה דרבי אבהו teaches that a son may feed his father pheasant and still be driven from עולם הבא, while another son has his father grind at the millstone. The teaching continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי, the son of רבי אבהו, taught: There is a son who feeds his father pheasant, and that drives him out of the world to come. And there is a son who makes his father grind at the millstone...
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: it is not only what a son gives his father that counts. The sentence is not finished here, and it continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Expensive food served the wrong way can still earn the son punishment, so the son's attitude matters. The contrast with the son who has his father do hard work sets up the second half, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught: introduces a teaching from the time of the תנאים
Drives him out of the world, meaning עולם הבא
Millstone, used for hard grinding work

steps.confusionAlert: The one driven out of the world is the son, not the father. And "the world" here means עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught:
There is one who feeds his father pheasants
and it drives him out of the world,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the son, and "the world" means עולם הבא.

phrases.english: and there is one who makes him grind at the millstone

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי אֲבִימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stories about דמא to a teaching about the inner quality of a son's service to his father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving a father lavish food does not by itself count as honoring him; a son can still lose עולם הבא. The contrasting case continues in the next section.
